sections.what: Santa Maria Hostel provides residential and outpatient substance use treatment for women, including pregnant and parenting women. Its Houston programs combine counseling, recovery support, childcare, housing assistance and career development. By accommodating children and providing ongoing support, it seeks to reduce barriers to recovery and family stability.
sections.monitoring: The original return describes a mixed continuum of women, children and family contacts, not unique treatment completions. The June 2025 notice says residential and outpatient capacity would fall to 60% after the Jacquelyn and detox closures, while Austin and other programs continue. Request current unique Houston treatment participants, completed dose, recovery follow-up, net resources and the latest operating budget.
sections.qualitative: Current services address childcare and housing barriers alongside substance use treatment. Three recent original returns support a comparable whole-recipient expense series. The organization publicly disclosed material funding cuts and treatment capacity changes. A recent closure reduced treatment capacity; current annual unique treatment completions are not verified. Recovery utility and net earnings effects are unsupported local priors, not measured causal effects. Whole-recipient costs include prevention, family services and Austin, while this numerator covers a narrow Houston women’s channel. No external trial is used to assert local effect size. Public funding and alternative providers may replace donation-funded care; this requires direct verification.
sections.cost: The conditional reference is $110.99 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 1.414508 clinical QALYs plus 0.088412 income equivalents. Full annual recognized cost is $16,681,490; $10,000 corresponds to 0.000901 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not a demonstrated gift response. The exposed union is 120.000 household proxies and the clinical subgroup is 60.000 adults. Clinical benefit is union × completion × utility × discounted finite years × geography. Financial successes and other exposed households are disjoint; each has one joint net log. Positive components receive the overlap adjustment before adding full negative components and subtracting full burdens. The resource success share is independent of clinical efficacy, so clinical null retains all resources and costs. Baseline consumption is positive even if reported income is zero. Gains are hypothetical otherwise-paid care or disposable resources after taxes, benefit withdrawal, new work expenses and substitution—not retail care values, gross salary or ordinary survivor earnings. One-off participation costs are incremental versus alternative care. Payer stress models distinct counterparty households; central external zero is an unknown-neutral partial-boundary reference, not observed zero or complete world benefit. Unrecognized partner/volunteer costs, broader portfolio benefits and harms, family spillovers and marginal funding response remain unknown.
sections.funding: Gross recognized expenses are FY2025 $16,681,490, FY2024 $15,639,260 and FY2023 $13,307,636, including direct event costs netted from revenue. Schedule D removed expense amounts match these event addbacks; no additional donated-service amount is identified. The series covers the entire recipient, not only Houston residential care. The organization announced a $15 million five-year public funding reduction; this does not prove a particular donation restores a bed or replaces that funding dollar-for-dollar.

model.costScope: Whole annual recipient recognized resources; limited clinical/resource numerator; marginal additional cost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .95 local share for the narrow Houston women cohort; Austin and other portfolio scope excluded.
model.formula: Union=N*unique*b; clinical=union*completion*q*discounted finite years minus full union harms. Financial=.5*people*discounted one-year log(1+joint net gain/baseline), local share once. Headline=10*C/(clinical+financial).
model.counterfactual: Alternative charity/public care, recovery supports, insurance eligibility, household behavior and funding replacement; additional response remains a prior.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded cost and service description; numerical clinical and disposable-resource effects are unsupported conditional hypotheses. Complete total EV remains unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Women’s treatment opportunities, finite symptom improvement and net household resource change; contacts are not completions.
